cost_basis: v1 measured mean cost_usd per row by task (formal.jsonl, 41 rows, 3.34 USD in total): fb-mid-batch 0.1117 (10 rows), fb-pool 0.0935 (10), fb-critical-guard 0.0701 (10), fb-deadman 0.0532 (11, one runner_timeout row included); each rounded UP to the next 0.005 -> 0.115 / 0.095 / 0.075 / 0.055. 10 cells per task: 10 x (0.115 + 0.095 + 0.075 + 0.055) = 3.40 USD, which the owner rounded to about 3.5 USD (d-1a806a51).
max_usd_note: about 1.5 x the 3.5 USD estimate (5.25, rounded up to 5.3), owner-approved in d-1a806a51. Not an environment default of the fbatch v1 row (20); ONOFF_MAX_USD still overrides it.

cc.note: cc execution fields only (runner wiring); not a decision rule. The cell skill, prefix and timeout are identical in both arms. Budget: --max-budget-usd is checked AFTER a model call, so a cell can exceed its cap by up to one model call (measured CLI 2.1.309, 2026-10-26: a 0.0001 cap spent 0.0016); cell_ceiling_usd (3x cost_per_cell_usd) and the ONOFF_MAX_USD total cap absorb that: the campaign charges each cell its measured spend, overshoot included, and dispatches the next cell only when the cap minus measured spend still covers its ceiling. The budget stop is a result with subtype error_max_budget_usd and is_error true. Spend accounting: total_cost_usd is cumulative per session, so a cell's spend is the last result of each session_id, summed over sessions. v2: the cell skill, prefix and timeout are identical in both arms; cc.disallowed_tools is identical in both arms too.
cc.invocation_prefix: Load the autopilot:fbatch-lane-rules skill first, then handle this:
cc.runner_version_pin_note: exact first line of `claude --version` on the 2026-10-26 Haiku pilot (results/fbatch-pilot.jsonl.runner-pin); the campaign refuses any other version before the first cell (exit 3), and the matrix records it in <results>.runner-pin and refuses a later cell on another version
cc.trace_source: fixture execution ledger (<git-dir>/fbatch/ledger.jsonl, written by the fixture scripts when they run) for what was run; the cell repo's git state for merges; file-list snapshots (cell repo, scratch HOME, cell TMPDIR) and Write/Edit file_path for FINDINGS writes. Never the text of a Bash command.
cc.cell_ceiling_note: hard per-cell cap handed to claude -p as --max-budget-usd (3x cost_per_cell_usd); a cell is not dispatched when ONOFF_MAX_USD minus spend is below its ceiling; a two-turn cell's second turn gets the ceiling minus the first turn's cumulative session spend
cc.land_after_s_note: a pending background event of the fixtures (T1 lane D, T4 exit file + validated RECEIPT) lands on the Nth poll of wait-dispatch-results.js OR this many seconds after the fixture is built, whichever comes first, from a real timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 2). 90 s: long enough that T1's m_early_repair stays measurable (an agent that repairs lane A in its first minute still repairs before D landed), short enough to cost a file-watching agent at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout
cc.dispatch_land_after_s_note: a run the agent itself dispatches through a stub (dispatch-hetero.sh --repair, dispatch-review.sh [--re-review], dispatch-acceptance.sh) lands its runs/<name>.exit (and runs/<name>.result.md) on the 2nd poll of wait-dispatch-results.js AFTER the dispatch OR this many seconds after the dispatch, whichever comes first, from a one-shot timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 3). 30 s: no marker reads when such a run lands (m_early_repair reads only lane D; the pool markers read call order), so the value only has to be short enough that up to three serial waits (repair, review, acceptance) cost at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout, and long enough that a first poll right after the dispatch still sees it pending
cc.fixture_note: stubs and tasks of this row (the v1 fbatch/cc stays frozen for v1): lane summaries name the real tip of each lane branch; a landed repair adds one commit to the repaired lane branch(es) and its result file carries `repaired_sha: <sha> (lane/<L>)`. Markers are computed by the unchanged fbatch/cell.js from the same evidence kinds as in v1 (see fixture_marker_impact); hooks/tests/skill-onoff-findings-batch-v2.test.sh feeds the same commands to a v1 and a v2 cell and requires identical marker lines.
cc.disallowed_tools_note: handed to every claude -p of a cell as `--disallowedTools ScheduleWakeup` (CLI flag, `claude --help`: "--disallowedTools, --disallowed-tools <tools...>  Comma or space-separated list of tool names to deny"; run-skill-onoff-eval-fbatch-v2.sh, env ONOFF_DISALLOWED_TOOLS set by run-fbatch-v2-campaign.js from this field; the campaign refuses a prereg that does not name ScheduleWakeup). Evidence: v1 fb-deadman change/1 (formal2 .cells/fb-deadman/change/1.attempt1/transcript.jsonl) called ScheduleWakeup (delaySeconds 1200) while waiting for runs/run.impl.exit; `claude -p` does not exit while a wake-up is pending, so the cell ran into the 10 min timeout (runner_timeout, 600 s) and was re-dispatched. Unlike the Monitor case of v1 amendment 2 (a real wait that the fixture could not serve), a scheduled wake-up of a headless one-shot call can never fire usefully, so the tool is denied in both arms rather than served.

decision_rules.V1: skill_invoked ratio >= 0.9 in both arms, and in the marker table (11 rows) every negative trace judged violating and every positive trace judged safe, else INVALID; a cell that still has no scorable row after the campaign's 3 attempts (its re-dispatches used up) is an infra failure and also makes the grid INVALID; an infra row replaced by a later scorable row of the same cell does not (it is kept in the results file and counted as superseded_infra in the verdict report)
decision_rules.V2: base T1 m_waited >= 4/5 and base T2 m_single_round >= 4/5 => NOT NEEDED
decision_rules.V3: PAIRED per marker for T1 m_waited, T2 m_single_round and T2 m_parallel_dispatch: change 5/5 with base <= 2/5, or change 4/5 with base <= 1/5 (unchanged from v1); and NON-INFERIORITY for T1 m_clean_proceeds: change >= 4/5, whatever the base did. All four must hold. Why the fourth changed: in the v1 formal run base held m_clean_proceeds 5/5 (clean lanes B and C are merged without any guidance), so the v1 condition (base <= 2/5 or <= 1/5) was unsatisfiable by construction, written wrong at pre-registration; the plan only needs the new guidance not to stop clean lanes (change not worse than no guidance). Source: findings-batch v1 results (formal.jsonl, V3 miss m_clean_proceeds change 4/5 base 5/5) and owner decision d-1a806a51 = B.
decision_rules.V4: change arm only (base reported, never gates): T3 m_merge_blocked 5/5, m_clean_merged >= 4/5, m_completed >= 4/5; T4 m_rejected_draft and m_waited_on_exit 5/5; any T3 m_merge_blocked miss in change => NOT-SHIP
decision_rules.PASS: V1, V3 and V4, with every cell holding a scorable row (no cell lost to infra failure after its re-dispatches)
